judged_text: Because the minimum schema never captures refresh_token (unknown keys are stripped), `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token` is always undefined and the code unconditionally overwrites it with the sentinel string "refresh_token". In Google CalendarService.ts (line ~99) this stripped object is persisted as the credential key via prisma.credential.update, permanently destroying the user's real refresh_token and all other credential fields; the OAuth credential can never be refreshed again and the integration is bricked for that user.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `parseRefreshTokenResponse` which, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is true, validates via `minimumTokenResponseSchema` (which does not include `refresh_token` and is not `.passthrough()`, so Zod will strip unknown keys). The function then executes `if (!refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token) { refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"; }`, guaranteeing a sentinel refresh token in that branch. In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the result of `parseRefreshTokenResponse(...)` is assigned to `key` and persisted directly via `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`, so the stored credential key will not contain the original refresh token (and may only contain the minimal parsed fields plus the sentinel). This is a verifiable data-loss/bricking risk introduced by the diff.
